What do you think will happen to Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich who was arrested for alleged spying in Russia? On July 19, 2024, the Regional Court in Yekaterinburg, Russia, sentenced American journalist Evan Gershkovich to 16 years in a maximum security colony. Russian human rights activist Vladimir Osechkin says that possibly he was baited by the FSB, to facilitate his arrest. 32-year-old journalist of WSJ was found guilty of espionage for collecting information about ‘Uralvagonzavod’, which is a factory that makes tanks for the Russian army. The prosecutor asked for an 18-year sentence. Gershkovich pleaded “not guilty” and insisted that he was acting as a journalist, not a spy. The court hearings were held behind closed doors, as the prosecution alleged the information that Gershkovich was getting was a “state secret”. Only the judge, the prosecutor, the defendant and his lawyers were present. Journalists were allowed into the meeting room for a few minutes before the hearing commenced to take photos and videos. Gershkovich, with a shaved head, greeted his colleagues with a smile, but did not answer any questions. Journalists were also allowed into the courtroom for the announcement of the harsh verdict: 16 years in a maximum security prison. Evan Gershkovich was detained on March 29, 2023 in Yekaterinburg, where he arrived for the second time in a month, to continue his investigation for the next story. At the WSJ Gershkovich worked since January 2022 — he joined the respected media just a month before Russia invaded Ukraine. Since then, he authored several key news stories related to Russia and Ukraine. In early March 2023, weeks before his arrest in Russia, he and his colleagues released a story about the growing tensions between the founder of “Wagner” Yevgeny Prigozhin and the Kremlin elites. In particular, the material stated, Kremlin officials turned to Russian President Vladimir Putin with a request to “rein in” Prigozhin, who criticized the Russian Ministry of Defense. Gershkovich was also one of the authors of a high-profile WSJ article about how Putin’s entourage may be hiding truthful information from him about the war in Ukraine. Putin receives a written report from the front every morning, however, the reports emphasize Russia army’s successes, and failures are tuned down. The reports are also delayed for several days, because they have to pass filters of the FSB and the Security Council, as well as get a personal stamp of approval from Nikolai Patrushev (then the secretary of Russia’s Security Council), the article claimed. Gershkovich's materials before his arrest in March 2023 were devoted to the worsening prospects for the Russian economy, the situation around Bakhmut, the visit to Moscow of China’s leader Xi Jinping and protests over the bill on "foreign agents" in Georgia. According to the photographer who worked with Gershkovich, he was collecting material for an article about how people in Russian regions perceive the war, for which he visited Yekaterinburg and Nizhny Tagil, and planned to go to other cities. The media wrote that Gershkovich was also interested in activities of the “Wagner”, including recruitment and cemeteries of the deceased fighters. At his court process, Gershkovich did not admit guilt and insisted that his research was purely journalistic. Evan Gershkovich became the first American journalist in modern Russian history to be accused of espionage. The last time an American journalist had been detained in Russia on espionage charges was in 1986, when a “News & World Report” employee Nicholas Daniloff was arrested. Daniloff was exchanged 3 weeks later. Before his arrest, Gershkovich worked in Russia for about 6 years, since 2017. At the time of his detainment, he had been living in London but regularly traveled on business trips to Russia, where he worked as part of the WSJ's Moscow bureau. His parents Mikhail Gershkovich and Emma Milman were emigrants from the USSR, but Evan himself lived his entire life in America. Several journalists who were friends with Gershkovich said that they warned him that reporting in Russia on the topics he was picking was dangerous and he could be arrested. But obviously, he didn’t think so. Gershkovich’s name has been frequently mentioned as someone who could be exchanged to Russian spies and assassins, arrested in Europe and the USA. He is probably the highest profile American hostage held by Putin. Putin discussed exchanging Gershkovich in his interview to Tucker Carlson in February 2024. Putin wanted to get in exchange the FSB assassin Vadim Krasikov, who is imprisoned in Germany. In 2021, Vadim Krasikov was sentenced to life in prison for the murder of Chechen field commander Zelimkhan Khangoshvili in Berlin in 2019. Carlson said at the time that Putin needed to talk to Germans about it. Peculiarly, Gershkovich’s process wasn’t held in Moscow but 2 thousand kilometers away, in Yekaterinburg, where he was arrested — away from Russia’s capital, where most of the foreign correspondents reside. This obviously prevented many western ambassadors and embassy officials from attending the process, which they would likely do as a show of solidarity, if the court hearing was in Moscow. The only hope for Gershkovich to get out of the Russian prison is an agreement for an exchange, which Putin would probably only approve if his assassin Krasikov is released, and Germany doesn’t seem keen on that. Otherwise, Gershkovich may only hope to get out if Vladimir Putin, on whose order he was arrested (no doubt, such high profile arrest and prosecution would require the highest nod), is no longer the ruler of Russia. So, Gershkovich is likely to remain behind bars in Russia, as the locals call it, “for as long as Putin is alive.”

What does Putin wish to achieve? Despondent Putin in North Korea, silently wishing to reset the world order to October 2021, to the version of history where he never attempted to bully NATO into submission. Frankly, I think that at this point, even Vladimir Putin himself doesn’t know what he wishes to achieve — except for the magic ability to time travel and change his own actions in the past. His plan to bully NATO spectacularly backfired — and Russians are paying a huge price for it, which will be echoing through decades and generations. For starters, in just months after Putin ordered his troops to bomb Ukraine, Russia became the most sanctioned country in the world, in response to inhumane atrocities it inflicted on Ukrainians. Nothing that Putin did before had produced such results: For over 2 decades, Putin was getting more and more imperious, and the response to the atrocities he caused to peoples of neighboring countries wasn’t strong enough to stop him venturing further. Putin’s attack on Ukraine could have been successful: if in February 2022, president Zelenskyy took the Americans’ offer to evacuate, as the 65-km-long column of Russian tanks was rolling towards the Ukrainian capital and Russian paratroopers were landing at the Hostomel air field 30 km from Kyiv, then it would be “game over” for Ukraine. Instead, Zelenskyy uttered the famous phrase: “I need ammunition, not a ride.” Putin hoped to cause an “anti-Maidan coup” in Ukraine. His plan was to re-install the expired president Victor Yanukovich, who escaped to Russia in February 2014, after months of unrest in Kyiv (initially caused by Yanukovich’s reneging on his pre-election promise that Ukraine would join the EU) — and after Yanukovich helped Putin (by not acting in Ukraine’s defence) to take over Crimea. Victor Yanukovich was the 4th president of Ukraine (25 February 2010 – 22 February 2014), who infamously escaped to Russia, where he now lives. After the re-reinstatement of Yanukovich (the application for reinstatement had already been quietly filed in a Kyiv court weeks before the February 2022 invasion, so it could be processed within a day, once Kyiv was under the Russian control), a new “election” would be called, in which Putin’s relative Medvedchuk would be “elected” as the new president of Ukraine. The plan was prepared in a great detail. Putin just didn’t foresee one thing: that the Russian troops wouldn’t be able to take Kyiv. And that Zelenskyy would be able to command the support of 95% of the Ukrainian population and lead the defence (in December 2021 — 2 months before the invasion — Zelenskyy’s approval rating in Ukraine was only 30%). Putin didn’t realize how strongly Ukrainians were united against becoming a part of Russia that when he nearly reached an agreement with the Ukrainian government in March 2022, under which Ukraine would “conditionally surrender”, he decided to add “the right of veto” for Russia on what happens to Ukraine if it’s being invaded again. The agreement that Ukraine nearly signed in March 2022 — weeks into the Russian invasion — is now all but an impossible dream for Putin. He keeps returning to its conditions and crying about the spilled milk, how the bloodbath that followed “could be prevented” — if Ukraine only agreed that Russia would be forever its ruler. The infamous “Istanbul March 2022 agreements” (which had never been fully agreed on by both parties or signed) included: And to these conditions, which the Ukrainian government was considering — Putin decided to add Russia’s “right of veto” on military aid to Ukraine in case if it ever was invaded. Basically, setting Russia to face no resistance in Ukraine when the Russian troops invade again. Russia is always doing this. This has been Russia’s modus operandi since they became a state in 1991. The old USSR still had some decency on the international stage; the Russian Federation, led by the KGB-trained clique, has none. It is content with acting in the most untrustworthy and barbaric ways. After February 2022, the masks are off — and so are the gloves. Putin’s Russia stopped hiding its inhumane essence and is gleefully demonstrating its brutishness. Putin hopes that this will save him from being ousted by his own people, whom he has promised the glory of superiority over Europe and America. Meanwhile, the reality is that he has to bow to China — and even North Korea — to be able to supply his troops, which otherwise would be exterminated in Ukraine. The huge, mighty Russia is unable to even hold onto 18% of the Ukrainian territory, without being propped by a little dictatorship of North Korea. But Putin’s wish remains to rule the world. He just needs to finally take in full the Donetsk region in Ukraine — which the Russians are trying to capture for 12.5 years — and for the West to agree that he’s the perfect person to decide who is allowed to do what, on the global scale. I don’t know how about the West, but Ukrainians are certainly not going to just give Putin what is not his.

Why does Russia refuse to accept equal blame for the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and the start of WWII? Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact: German Foreign Minister Joachim von Ribbentrop (left), Soviet leader Joseph Stalin and USSR Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov (right) on August 23, 1939 in the Kremlin after signing the pact. Stalin made a toast after the ceremony: "I know how much the German people love their Fuhrer. Therefore, I want to drink to his health." On September 1, 1939 Germany’s attacked Poland. The Soviet Union attacked Poland on September 17, 1939. On September 22, Nazis and Soviets held a joint parade in Brest, celebrating their victory. In 1946, at the Nuremberg Trials, the former State Secretary of the German Foreign Ministry, Ernst von Weizsäcker, spoke about the existence of a secret additional protocol between the USSR and Germany. This was confirmed by other defendants, and one of the lawyers even wanted to read the text of this protocol, but he was not allowed: the USSR representatives called it a fake and said such a document never existed. In 1948, the secret protocol, based on photocopies of the German original that had not survived, was published in the US State Department collection "Nazi-Soviet Relations. 1939-1941". It also included the correspondence between Nazi and Soviet diplomats, which contained references to secret agreements. But the Soviet Union continued to claim that this was a falsification, that no additional secret appendix to the 1939 agreements ("On Non-Aggression" and "On Friendship and Borders") between the USSR and Germany existed. Moreover: in response to the publication by the State Department, Moscow published its own work titled "Falsifiers of History". But it did not contain a single complete copy of a document, only a few fragments. Stalin didn’t want to be blamed in starting the World War with Hitler, and used the status of the USSR as one of the “victors of WW2” to suppress this extremely important information. Molotov, who signed the non-aggression pact and the secret protocol to it, denied its existence until his death in 1986. Minister of Foreign Affairs of the USSR Vyacheslav Molotov in Berlin, November 14, 1940. It was hard to prove that such a document existed: one party that signed it (Hitler's Germany) no longer existed, and the other (the Soviet Union) denied that it existed at all, and had no intention of publishing it. Only in 1989, the Soviet leaders admitted that such secret protocol existed, on request of representatives of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. A copy of the German document was published in the USSR. The actual copy of the secret protocol in Russian was first kept in Stalin's safe and then in the archive of the Central Committee of the Communist Party. In 1992, after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the archive of the Communist Party was declassified and the secret protocol was discovered. From that moment, the existence of a secret additional treaty to the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact had become a reliably recognized fact not only in the West, not only in the Baltic countries, Moldova and Ukraine, but also in Russia itself. But now, Putin’s propaganda downplays the importance of the secret agreement between Hitler and Stalin how they would divide Europe, and overemphasizes that it was a non-aggression pact, which allowed the USSR 2 more years without the war. In the next 400 days, hundreds of thousands of people were killed, millions sent to GULAG. About 700,000 people were shot, after they signed confessions that they planned to damage the Soviet state — signed under torture. More than 1.7 million people were arrested and given various prison terms; hundreds of thousands of them never returned from the GULAG. There were no trials, not even an appearance of trials. Instead, the NKVD gave the power to sentence people to death or decades of GULAG to "special trios." “The trio” included the head of the local NKVD, the head of the regional communist party committee, and the prosecutor. The accused didn’t have attorneys. There were no lawyers. There was no public. Just the accused, the trio, and the prison guards. Sentences were given within minutes, one by one: guilty. The Soviet conveyor of death. Some death lists were approved by Stalin himself. The USSR dictator personally sanctioned the execution of more than 40,000 people. There were already purges in the first half of the 1930s: in 1934, 80,000 people were convicted in OGPU-NKVD cases. And let’s not forget the man-made famines of 1932–33 that killed millions. Many thought that the purge would not affect them, that the NKVD came for ”saboteurs” and “spies” — that if you were a model citizen, obeying every Stalin’s order, satisfying all his whims, then you would be okay. And then suddenly millions of these “model citizens” found themselves signing “admissions of guilt” under horrendous torture. Their wives were either shot or sent to GULAG, as were their teenage children. Minor kids were sent to orphanages or adopted by families of other law-obedient Soviet citizens. Kids of “enemies of the state”. No names — just numbers. Stalin didn’t invent “The Red Terror”. It was invented by Vladimir Lenin — the father of October 1917 Bolsheviks’ coup. Lenin ordered to kill anyone who was against “the proletarian revolution”. And anyone who potentially could be against it — just in case. The horror of the Red Terror is realistically conveyed in the Russian-made film "Chekist" (1992). It should have been shown to Russian schoolkids. It wasn’t. Now it’s too late and Putin’s goons won’t allow it. Putin’s goons are making a hero and “the father of the nation” out of Stalin, erect monuments to him. Hundreds of thousands of Russian men are sent to slaughter in Ukraine — 1,000 of them are ending dead, maimed or wounded every single day. And all these Russian citizens of today behave like the Soviet citizens of 1930s, they are sure that if they are being “good patriots”, they will be okay. Russia is falling into the same pattern. Again.
